> الأصل في البيانات المفتوحة أنها مجانية، ولا يجوز للمستخدم بيعها أو ترخيصها أو تأجيرها.

*"Open data is by default free of charge, and the user may not sell it, license it, or rent it."*

That's the whole clause. There's no "...unless you add value" or "...except for derivative commercial products" anywhere in this document — that carve-out isn't in the primary text. It reads as a flat prohibition on selling, sublicensing, or renting the data, full stop. The rest of the summary checks out: attribution is required (§6, must cite the source), and §4's prohibited-uses list does include acting against Saudi law, public order, and what it calls "مخالف للدين الاسلامي" — contrary to Islamic teaching — alongside political misuse.

That's not something I should resolve by inference between two PDFs; it's precisely the kind of ambiguity a lawyer reads, not an AI summary.

# SFDA / SDAIA Open Data License — research note, 2026-09-14

**Status: does not change the Group D / quarantined classification.** Recorded
so the next person doesn't re-run the same search and doesn't mistake "a
licence exists" for "this dataset carries it."

**Update, same day:** Yazeed supplied the actual PDF (`~/Documents/
Open_Data_License_Ar.pdf`, saved here as reference — "رخصة استخدام البيانات
المفتوحة" / Open Data Use License, SDAIA, version 2.0, March 2023). This
supersedes the web-search-only findings below with a primary-source read.

**What the document itself says, verbatim, page 3 (§1, licence summary),
third line, before anything else:**

> ينطبق هذا على: مجموعات البيانات المفتوحة المنشورة في منصة
> (open.data.gov.sa).

*"This applies to: open datasets published on the (open.data.gov.sa)
platform."*

The rest of Yazeed's original claim checks out against the primary text:
§5 grants exactly extraction, redistribution, reuse, modification, adaptation,
and creating derivative/shared datasets, worldwide and non-exclusive, with no
commercial exclusion; §2 (Introduction) names it explicitly as an
implementation of the **Open Data Commons Attribution License**; §6.1
(Notices) requires attribution — carrying the licence terms forward, a URI
back to the licensed dataset, and retaining any copyright/database-right
notices already on it.

**So: real licence, generous terms, confirmed from SDAIA's own document — but
scoped by that document's own words to datasets published through
`open.data.gov.sa`.** It is a portal licence, not a blanket grant over
everything any Saudi government body publishes anywhere. Nothing in this PDF
names the Saudi Food Composition Tables, and it contains no appendix or list
of covered datasets/organisations — that linkage can only be established by
finding SFCT actually listed on the portal (or a written SFDA statement
invoking this licence for it), not by this document alone.

**Second update, same day:** Yazeed supplied a second SDAIA PDF —
`Open_Data_Terms_Of_Use_Ar.pdf`, "الشروط والأحكام لمنصة البيانات المفتوحة"
("Terms and Conditions of the Open Data Platform"), first version, dated
2023-03-21. This is a different document from the licence above: it governs
using the *website* (registration, prohibited platform conduct, the
platform's own IP in its branding/UI, liability, jurisdiction), not data
content rights, except for one clause.

**§6 (Intellectual Property Rights), verbatim:**

> الأصل في البيانات المفتوحة أنها مجانية، ولا يجوز للمستخدم بيعها أو
> ترخيصها أو تأجيرها.

*"Open data is by default free of charge, and the user may not sell it,
license it, or rent it."*

That is the entire clause — no "...unless value is added" or "...except
derivative commercial products" qualifier appears anywhere in this document.
A paraphrase Yazeed was given (via an AI tool, again citation-marked)
asserted that raw reselling is barred but "commercial applications" and
"value-add" derivatives are explicitly permitted; **that distinction is not
in SDAIA's text** — it is an inference the summarising tool added, not a
quote. Attribution (§6, cite the source) and the prohibited-use list (§4:
against Saudi law, public order, and "مخالف للدين الاسلامي" — contrary to
Islamic teaching, alongside political misuse) do check out as stated.

**This complicates rather than resolves the picture.** The Use License (v2.0)
grants broad redistribution/derivative rights with no commercial exclusion
found in its text; this Terms of Use flatly bars selling, licensing or
renting the data. Whether packaging SFDA-derived values inside a paid app
counts as "selling the data" under §6, versus building a permitted
value-added derivative under the licence's §5, is a real tension between two
of SDAIA's own documents — exactly the kind of question for the law-firm
route in the 2026-09-13 handoff, not something to infer from the PDFs alone.
It is also, again, moot until SFCT is confirmed to be published under either
document at all: neither names it, lists it, or references a dataset
catalogue.

## What prompted this

Yazeed supplied a claim (via an AI research tool, citation-marked) that SFDA
data is covered by "the Saudi Data & AI Authority (SDAIA) Open Data License
(Version 2.0)": commercial use explicitly permitted, attribution required,
referencing the ODC Attribution License.

## What was checked, and what came back

1. **The licence itself is real.** A Wikipedia summary of `open.data.gov.sa`
   cites a PDF titled *"Open Data License En v2.0"* hosted on that portal, and
   describes it in terms consistent with the claim: datasets on the Saudi Open
   Data Platform are covered by an ODC-Attribution-style licence permitting
   use, modification and sharing with attribution. **I could not fetch the
   licence PDF itself** — `open.data.gov.sa` and `od.data.gov.sa` both reject
   automated fetches (WAF "Request Rejected" / redirect-then-block). Nothing
   in this note is a verbatim quote of the licence text; it is one step short
   of that.
2. **The licence attaches to datasets published *through* the Saudi Open Data
   Portal** (`od.data.gov.sa`), not to everything a Saudi government body
   publishes anywhere. SFDA does have an organisation presence on that portal
   — food-establishment licensing lists, ICOSMA/cosmetics registrations,
   medical-device registrations are all there, each presumably under this
   licence.
3. **The Saudi Food Composition Tables do not appear in that listing.** A
   search of the SFDA organisation's dataset page on `od.data.gov.sa`, and
   separate searches for the Arabic title ("جداول تراكيب الأغذية السعودية")
   restricted to that domain, returned nothing. The SFCT PDFs Almanac holds
   were retrieved directly from `sfda.gov.sa`'s news/press pages
   (`sfda.gov.sa/en/news/5521776`, `sfda.gov.sa/sites/default/files/2026-04/
   SFCT-E.pdf`) — outside the open-data portal — and, per
   `metadata/sfda/SOURCE.md`, the PDF itself states no licence.
4. A search snippet describes an SFDA regulations page
   (`sfda.gov.sa/en/regulations/5521782`, titled "Saudi Food Composition
   Table") as tagged **"Open data"** on SFDA's own site. I could not load that
   page directly (404 to this session's fetcher — likely JS-rendered or
   geo/bot-gated) to see what "Open data" means there: a link to the
   od.data.gov.sa listing (in which case point 3 already says it isn't
   there), a bare label with no defined terms, or something else. **Someone
   with a normal browser should open this page and report what it actually
   says and links to.**

## Conclusion

The standing rule in `LICENSES.md` applies exactly as written: *"publicly
accessible ≠ open source"*, *"government data ≠ public domain"*, *"downloadable
≠ redistributable."* A real, favourable licence existing on a government
portal does not establish that this specific PDF is published under it. That
link is the missing piece, not a formality — SFDA visibly does put some of its
datasets on the open-data portal under this licence and, on current evidence,
has not put this one there.

**Recorded, not concluded: still `unclear`, still Group D, still quarantined.**

## What would actually resolve this — cheapest to slowest

1. Open `sfda.gov.sa/en/regulations/5521782` in a real browser and see what its
   "Open data" tag links to or cites. If it links to an `od.data.gov.sa`
   dataset page for SFCT, that page's own licence badge is the evidence —
   screenshot or save it here.
2. Browse (not search-index) the SFDA organisation's full dataset list on
   `od.data.gov.sa` by hand, across pages, in both languages — the automated
   search here may simply have missed a differently-titled entry.
3. Absent either: the enquiry in `licenses/sfda/ENQUIRY-DRAFT.md` still stands,
   and per the 2026-09-13 handoff, this is also worth Yazeed's law-firm
   connection confirming directly with SFDA/SDAIA before anything ships.

# Handoff — Almanac nutrition module, next steps

**Context:** Almanac is a free body-monitor app (sleep/food/energy/activity).
The 2026-09-13 handoff's calorie-database build order is done: nutrient
dictionary, USDA/CIQUAL/CoFID/AFCD extraction and canonicalisation, the
licence-guard bundle step, and the AlmanacCore wiring (migration, importer,
catalog, calorie calculation). None of that is repeated here — read the
referenced docs directly.

**Where the code is:** committed on `codex/manual-entry`, commit `9445a51`.
**Not pushed** — nothing has gone to a remote or been opened as a PR.

## What's actually built and verified

| | |
|---|---|
| Pipeline | `tools/nutrition/` (Python 3.14 + stdlib, openpyxl, lxml). `python3 -m almanac_nutrition all` runs extract→canonicalise→union→bundle for every source; `qa` re-reads every raw cell independently; `fixture` regenerates the cross-language test fixture. |
| Bundle | `~/ALManac-food-data/build/almanac.sqlite`, schema v1. 8,354 foods, 49,036 values, groups A/B only. Not in git — it's a lake artefact, rebuild it from `tools/nutrition` whenever needed. |
| AlmanacCore | `LicenceGroup.native` (group N), `Migration008_NutritionReference` (`nutrition_*` tables), `NutritionReferenceImporter` (re-asserts the licence guard before writing anything), `NutritionCatalog` (food/values/bases/search), `GeneralAtwater`/`EnergyEstimate` (4/4/9/7 kcal/g, publisher-reported fallback). |
| Tests | Swift: `source env.sh && swift test` → 115 tests, 114 pass, 1 skipped (opt-in `NutritionRealBundleTests`, enable with `ALMANAC_NUTRITION_BUNDLE=~/ALManac-food-data/build/almanac.sqlite`). Python: `cd tools/nutrition && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` → 101 pass; add `ALMANAC_NUTRITION_INTEGRATION=1` for the real-lake checks. |
| Docs | `docs/features/nutrition.md` (what shipped, coverage, energy-vs-publisher numbers), `tools/nutrition/README.md` (pipeline contract — read this before touching any source module), `~/ALManac-food-data/PROCESSING-LOG-2026-09-13.md` (findings in the data), `docs/implementation-status.md` (updated). |

QA is clean: 0 fidelity problems against the raw files, 0 tokens (`Tr`/`N`/
`traces`/`-`) turned into a number, 0 unexplained zeros, 0 licence problems.

## Two things genuinely blocked — not build tasks, don't re-attempt them

1. **Saudi/Gulf dish data for Almanac-native (`almanac:`) entries.** The
   schema, licence group N, and bundle slot all exist and are tested (see the
   `almanac:fixture-dish` rows in `tools/nutrition/fixtures/bundle_v1.sql`).
   What's missing is the actual dish data — recipes, personal knowledge, or a
   chosen reference. Has to come from Yazeed.
2. **SFDA licence question.** Long thread on 2026-09-14, fully written up at
   `~/ALManac-food-data/licenses/sfda/SDAIA-OPEN-DATA-LICENSE-RESEARCH-2026-09-14.md`.
   Short version: SDAIA's real Open Data Use License v2.0 and Terms of Use
   PDFs were read primary-source; the terms are favourable (attribution-based,
   and Almanac being free resolves the sale/rental prohibition in the Terms of
   Use); but **neither document names or lists the Saudi Food Composition
   Tables**, and no evidence was found that SFCT is actually published through
   `open.data.gov.sa` rather than just `sfda.gov.sa`'s press pages. SFDA stays
   **Group D, quarantined, unclear** until that specific link is confirmed —
   by finding SFCT listed on the open-data portal, a written SFDA reply (draft
   already sits at `~/ALManac-food-data/licenses/sfda/ENQUIRY-DRAFT.md`), or
   law-firm sign-off. Don't reopen the research — read the file, then either
   the confirmation exists or it doesn't.

## Suggested build order for next session

Nothing here depends on either blocked item above. Proceed under these unless
Yazeed redirects:

1. **Portions and household measures.** Processing Design v0.1 §4 already
   worked out that this is solved for Group A/B without the (Group D) FAO
   density database: USDA's `food_portion` table (`fdc_id` + `measure_unit` →
   `gram_weight`, CC0, already in the extracted USDA CSVs) and CoFID's
   `Specific gravity` / `Edible proportion` columns (`1.2 Factors` sheet,
   already extracted, not yet canonicalised). Add a `nutrition_portion` table
   and canonicalise both into it. This is the natural next data slice and
   reuses everything already built.
2. **Food logging.** The catalog can answer "what's in this food" and "how
   many calories" — nothing yet records "the user ate 150 g of this." Follow
   the existing per-module-table pattern (`lab_*`, `health_sample`): a
   `nutrition_log` table, source-scoped identity, revision-friendly, feeding
   the shared timeline the same way Laboratory and HealthSampleStore already
   do. `mattpocock-skills:tdd` for this, same as the reference-database work.
3. **Native manual-entry scaffolding**, mirroring Laboratory's
   (`FieldEdit`, `ManualEntryTests`, audited edits): the *mechanism* for
   entering an `almanac:` dish (per-100g values, or a recipe of other
   reference foods that `GeneralAtwater`-style logic reduces to per-100g) can
   be built and tested now, entirely independent of having real dish content.
   The moment dish data arrives, only data entry remains — not a design or
   schema task.

Optional, parallel, not code: a re-review of the Group C/D quarantine list in
`~/ALManac-food-data/LICENSES.md` now that "Almanac is free" is confirmed —
some entries were quarantined citing commercial redistribution specifically
(e.g. CC BY-NC-SA sources), which a free app may clear; others (ODbL
share-alike, request-only access) are unaffected by price and shouldn't be
re-litigated. Flagged, not started — say if you want it done.

## Suggested skills

- `mattpocock-skills:tdd` — for the portions table and food-logging module,
  same red-green-refactor pattern as the reference database.
- `data:explore-data` / `data:sql-queries` — for the USDA `food_portion` /
  CoFID Factors canonicalisation.
- `data:validate-data` — QA pass on portion gram-weights before wiring them
  in, same discipline as the nutrient QA pass.

## Don't do

- Don't re-run the SFDA/SDAIA licence research — it's written up, read it.
- Don't touch USDA Branded Foods, SR Legacy, FNDDS, Frida, or Oman FCT 2024
  without a reason; they're deliberately out of this phase.
- Don't ship or use SFDA, NEVO, TBCA, IFCT, FAO/INFOODS, Bahrain, Tunisia, or
  Open Food Facts data — all still Group C/D, quarantined.
- Don't open with clarifying questions about the two blocked items above;
  build the next-session order and flag anything that comes up.

## References

- `tools/nutrition/README.md` — pipeline contract, read before touching a source module
- `docs/features/nutrition.md` — what shipped
- `docs/implementation-status.md` — current test counts and toolchain notes
- `~/ALManac-food-data/PROCESSING-LOG-2026-09-13.md` — findings in the raw data
- `~/ALManac-food-data/licenses/sfda/SDAIA-OPEN-DATA-LICENSE-RESEARCH-2026-09-14.md` — the licence thread, in full
- `~/ALManac-food-data/PROCESSING_DESIGN.md` §4 — the portions/density-database reasoning for item 1 above

No secrets, credentials, or personal data in scope for this handoff.
